name: ComputerUse.space

modes.label: ThinkCentre 8 GB planned
modes.note: Advertised $24.99 per 30 days, not a 730-hour month. Host has 8 GB installed RAM and planned 80 GB customer storage; guest RAM and CPU unknown. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: ThinkCentre 16 GB planned
modes.note: Advertised $39.99 per 30 days. Host has 16 GB installed RAM and planned 150 GB customer storage; guest RAM and CPU unknown. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

modes.label: ThinkCentre annual prepay (planned)
modes.commit_note: $239.90 / $383.90 prepaid per calendar year (= $19.99 / $31.99 per month); 20% off twelve 30-day payments

plans.name: Prelaunch reservation terms
plans.note: No purchasable inventory or live payments (/api/v1/stock: available 0, purchases_enabled false). Rental targets $24.99/$39.99 per 30 days, prepaid credit, auto-renew from balance; annual prepay $239.90/$383.90 per calendar year. Up to 100 computers per order.

features.ip_note: Desktops run as Proxmox VMs on rented owner hosts (Lenovo ThinkCentre), with a Hetzner relay fallback for streaming; egress IP type undocumented. Prelaunch: customer rentals pending.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Explicit prelaunch: account/management APIs and a Linux owner pilot exist, but customer rentals, live payments and verified inventory are not open. Modes are beta-only.

Installed host RAM is not fully available guest RAM. Customers do not receive Proxmox host administration. Windows readiness, editing performance, backups, proxies and storage add-ons need verification.

Billing is prepaid credit (top-ups); each rental auto-renews from balance every 30 days; insufficient credit queues suspension. Paid term starts when provisioning is confirmed ready. 30-day term means ~12.17 renewals per calendar year (1.4% above a 730h month).
Windows is listed as plan software in the stock API (Standard: Windows; Creator: Windows, CapCut) but docs say Linux is the initial target and a Windows surcharge has not been finalized.
Terminal/file API, file transfers, templates/clone/resize, proxies, NAS/S3 backups, SSO/SLA are not deployed (roadmap/proposal). Proxies, storage upgrades, paid software billed separately (unpriced).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: | Reboot or stop | Disk remains; running processes are not retained |
snapshot_auto.note: Stop/reboot only keeps the local SSD guest disk (that is persistent_disk); no automatic snapshot or memory checkpoint on stop/idle. There is no idle auto-stop at all: rentals are always-on 30-day dedicated hosts. Backups (NAS/S3) are an architecture proposal only.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: | Templates, clone, resize, multi-screen | Roadmap | Capacity-aware runtime implementation |
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint in the OpenAPI file, which the docs say lists exactly the implemented handlers ('All paths in that document correspond to current handlers.', https://computeruse.space/docs-source/api.md). Templates/cloning are roadmap; a clone would need a second physical host. Proxmox VM snapshots exist under the hood (mentioned only in cleanup/retention context) but customers get no Proxmox administration.

harness_api.quote: | Managed model routing / agent threads | Roadmap | Provider integration, metering and retention |
harness_api.note: The opposite direction exists: a stdio MCP bridge (python -m computeruse.mcp) and REST API let an external agent (Boardly, OpenClaw, Hermes) manage rentals and drive the desktop via screenshots/mouse/keyboard leases. Nothing starts or streams an agent harness inside the guest; no terminal/exec API either ('Terminal/file API and audio | Not deployed'). Boardly (separate product) has take-over/give-back of the desktop, not a harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: All paths in that document correspond to current handlers. Planned runtime APIs are documented separately and are not included as if implemented.
egress_allowlist.note: Implemented API has no network-policy endpoints (groups: accounts, keys, rentals, billing, proxies catalog/quote, admin, desktops). Operator-side tenant isolation is only a design goal: 'Each customer guest should have its own isolated network boundary. Deny access to the operator's LAN, host/hypervisor services, other guests and storage administration.' (proxies.md); pilot runs on an unmanaged switch. No customer-configurable allow/deny list.

egress_http_rules.quote: All paths in that document correspond to current handlers. Planned runtime APIs are documented separately and are not included as if implemented.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP-level egress rules implemented or planned in docs. Supplier-backed outbound proxies are 'Catalog/quote foundation · Supplier activation pending' (a quote does not attach a proxy); these are IP-rotation proxies, not policy rules.

secret_proxy.quote: Agents still need model-provider credentials and budgets. ComputerUse's rental price does not pay for unlimited tokens. Prefer short-lived scoped secrets, task budgets and approval for consequential actions.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy and no secret store. Hosted agents keep their API keys inside the guest ('Its state, channels, API keys and learned skills then become part of the customer workspace'); templates doc says 'Inject customer secrets at provisioning time' (roadmap). Managed model routing is roadmap. No non-HTTP coverage.

volume_attach.quote: | NAS/S3 storage and disaster recovery | Architecture proposal | Hardware/provider configuration and restore drills |
volume_attach.note: Only the fixed local-SSD guest disk (80 GiB Standard / 150 GiB Creator). storage-backups.md: 'Architecture proposal · No storage provider connected'. Storage upgrades mentioned elsewhere as separately billed add-ons but unpriced/not implemented.

volume_shared.quote: A NAS can store image backups, approved customer file shares and media projects. Give every tenant a separate authorized share and quota. Do not mount a global share inside every guest.
volume_shared.note: Proposal only (page status 'Architecture proposal · No storage provider connected'); a per-tenant NAS share could in future be mounted by several of one customer's computers, but nothing is implemented. virtual-computers.md: NAS/S3 'Neither is automatically a shared customer folder.'

isolation.quote: Every company and partner rental machine must run Proxmox VE as its always-on host operating system. A rental receives a new virtual machine created from an approved clean template.
isolation.note: Proxmox VE virtualizes guests with QEMU/KVM; each rental is a full VM on a dedicated physical host, not a shared-kernel container or microVM.

image_oci.quote: Build clean, versioned application images containing software and configuration, not customer browser sessions, API keys or personal files.
image_oci.note: not offered: the product boots Proxmox VM templates (roadmap for cloning), not customer-supplied Docker/OCI images.

anti_bot.quote: A proxy is not permission to violate website terms or perform unauthorized collection, fraud or abuse. Do not describe it as untraceability or guaranteed access to a blocked service.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; ComputerUse is a dedicated desktop rental, and its own docs disclaim anti-detection/untraceability framing.

captcha_solving.quote: GIVE YOUR AGENT SOMEWHERE TO WORK. Dedicated computers. Room for your ideas.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a general-purpose dedicated desktop, not a scraping/CAPTCHA-solving service).

ssh.quote: Terminal/file API and audio | Not deployed | Separate permissions and transports
ssh.note: No terminal or shell access of any kind (SSH or otherwise) is deployed yet; docs also stress customers never receive host SSH credentials.

snapshot.quote: Templates, clone, resize, multi-screen | Roadmap | Capacity-aware runtime implementation
snapshot.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint exists in the implemented API; only the persistent guest disk survives stop/reboot, no memory or on-demand snapshot capability.

fork.quote: Clone: A clone needs another available host for a dedicated rental. It cannot create physical capacity out of the first ThinkCentre.
fork.note: Cloning is explicitly roadmap-only, gated on physical capacity and licensing.

fork_running.quote: Clone: A clone needs another available host for a dedicated rental.
fork_running.note: Not implemented; cloning at all is roadmap, let alone cloning a running machine.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Clone: Copy only authorized customer data, create new credentials and require a separate paid allocation.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No cloning capability exists, so no memory-preserving fork exists either.

pause_resume.quote: Stopping renewal preserves the current paid term; stopping an agent does not stop renewal.
pause_resume.note: Rentals are always-on 30-day dedicated hosts billed on a fixed renewal cadence; there is no pause feature that reduces or halts billing.

wake_on_request.quote: Shut down guest | Stops processes and normal RAM state | Persistent disk stays
wake_on_request.note: No sleep/wake-on-request mechanism is described; dedicated hosts are always-on for the paid term.

persistent_disk.quote: | Reboot or stop | Disk remains; running processes are not retained |
persistent_disk.note: Guest disk (local SSD) persists across reboot/stop for the life of the rental.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Each paid dedicated rental reserves one Proxmox host for one customer VM.
auto_stop_idle.note: Dedicated hosts run continuously for the 30-day/annual paid term; no idle auto-stop is offered.

live_resize.quote: Moving from an 8 GB host to a 16 GB host requires free compatible capacity and a migration/reboot workflow. Do not offer unlimited instant vertical scaling or promise live migration without testing it.
live_resize.note: Resize requires moving to different physical hardware plus a reboot; explicitly not live/instant.

agent_harnesses.quote: Build clean, versioned application images containing software and configuration, not customer browser sessions, API keys or personal files.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: guest images are clean OS templates; coding-agent harnesses are not preinstalled. Integration guides (Boardly/OpenClaw/Hermes) connect external agents via MCP instead.

own_agent_api.quote: Use the agent where it runs best, and give it a scoped computer connection. Remote agent: Boardly, OpenClaw or Hermes runs elsewhere.
own_agent_api.note: ComputerUse provides infrastructure (desktop + MCP/API) for third-party agents (Boardly, OpenClaw, Hermes); it does not ship its own task/computer-use agent.

public_ipv4.quote: Boardly uses the direct local connection when your computer can reach the desktop... If the direct route is unavailable, the server connection takes over.
public_ipv4.note: Desktop access is brokered via ComputerUse's HTTPS/WebRTC relay and control API, not via a public IPv4 address assigned to the machine.

inbound_https.quote: All paths in that document correspond to current handlers. Planned runtime APIs are documented separately and are not included as if implemented.
inbound_https.note: not offered: no documented feature exposes arbitrary services running inside the guest via an HTTPS URL; only the management/desktop-control API and relay streaming exist.

ingress_rules.quote: Implemented endpoint groups | Accounts, Keys, Rentals, Billing, Proxies, Administration
ingress_rules.note: No network-policy/ingress-control endpoints exist in the implemented API surface.

gpu.quote: Plan | Installed host RAM | Customer storage target | Base rental | Annual prepayment ... Standard 8 GB ... Creator 16 GB
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's current scope; plans are defined by CPU/RAM/disk only, and desktop-control.md states 'These are system RAM allocations, not dedicated GPU/video memory.'

windows.quote: Linux is the initial deployment target. Windows availability and any surcharge depend on the selected Windows product, hosting entitlements, hardware compatibility and tested image. A Windows surcharge has not been finalized.
windows.note: Windows is planned but not currently offered/verified; Linux is the initial target.

macos.quote: Use a 64-bit Intel or AMD computer with virtualization enabled... ARM computers and Apple Silicon are not supported.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; hosts are x86 Proxmox machines, Apple hardware explicitly unsupported.

arm64.quote: ARM computers and Apple Silicon are not supported.
arm64.note: Explicitly unsupported for host hardware, so no ARM guest offering exists.

self_host.quote: Choose 2 for a partner host, enter the host ID from your account and its private one-use pairing code.
self_host.note: not offered: the 'become a host' program contributes a machine to ComputerUse's own managed rental pool for revenue share; it is not a self-hosted private deployment of the product.

byoc.quote: Every company and partner rental host must run Proxmox VE. Reserve one host per customer and expose a managed guest VM.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the model is dedicated physical hardware managed by ComputerUse, not deployment into a customer's own cloud account.

soc2.quote: This page is a product-policy draft, not an assertion of certification or a completed legal privacy notice.
soc2.note: not offered: prelaunch product; no SOC 2 report or compliance page is published, and privacy/security policy is explicitly still a draft.

hipaa.quote: This page is a product-policy draft, not an assertion of certification or a completed legal privacy notice.
hipaa.note: not offered: no HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere in docs; prelaunch product with only draft privacy policy.

sso.quote: Enterprise SSO, SLA and regional fleets | Roadmap | Commercial and operational readiness
sso.note: Explicitly listed as roadmap, not implemented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Enterprise SSO, SLA and regional fleets | Roadmap | Commercial and operational readiness
eu_data_residency.note: Regional fleets (which would enable region/EU choice) are roadmap; hosts today are specific US/company-owned ThinkCentres, not region-selectable.

max_session_h.quote: Each paid dedicated rental reserves one Proxmox host for one customer VM.
max_session_h.note: Dedicated hosts are rented continuously for the paid term (30 days / annual) with no session-length limit; the machine runs until the rental ends or is stopped.

egress_ip_type.quote: Use a 64-bit Intel or AMD computer with virtualization enabled, at least 8 GB RAM, an internal disk of at least 64 GiB and wired Internet access.
egress_ip_type.note: Rental hosts are individual company/partner-owned ThinkCentre desktops enrolled from wherever they physically sit, each on its own single Internet connection ('One NAS, one switch, one ISP or one site creates a shared failure risk.', enterprise.md) rather than colocated in a datacenter. Guest egress therefore rides the host's own business/residential ISP link, not a cloud/datacenter IP block. A Hetzner relay is documented only as a streaming/viewer fallback, not as the VM's general egress path.

open_source.quote: A new home for your AI agents ... Dedicated ThinkCentres, predictable rental pricing, and a place for your agents to get things done.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ComputerUse is a proprietary hosted rental service with a private management backend, a downloadable boot ISO for enrolling host hardware, and a source package used only to run its own MCP bridge/API client locally; no OSI license or public source repository for the core service is published anywhere in the docs or site.

guest_firewall.quote: Every company and partner rental machine must run Proxmox VE as its always-on host operating system. A rental receives a new virtual machine created from an approved clean template. Customers access that guest desktop through ComputerUse; they do not receive the hypervisor administrator account.
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is qemu-kvm (a full Proxmox VM dedicated to one customer, not a shared-kernel container). Docs distinguish the hypervisor admin account (withheld) from the customer's own guest desktop (given), implying customers have ordinary admin/root control of their own dedicated guest OS, where nftables/iptables would work normally. Not independently confirmed by a docs statement about guest firewall rules specifically.

usage_api.quote: List and inspect: Use `GET /api/v1/account` with `account:read`. The returned `rentals` include the rental ID, state, plan, amount, term, renewal preference and period boundaries.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; ComputerUse bills by fixed plan prices per 30-day term or annual term. GET /api/v1/account returns per-rental data including amount/cost for each dedicated VM. Each rental is a dedicated physical ThinkCentre host, so granularity is per-sandbox/per-rental.

persist_scope.quote: | Reboot or stop | Disk remains; running processes are not retained |
persist_scope.note: The whole disk survives a stop, installed packages included.

locations_quote: Enterprise SSO, SLA and regional fleets | Roadmap | Commercial and operational readiness
